source_text: Καὶ εῦξατο Ἱεμθάε τῷ Κυφίῳ. Εἰ Πνεῦμα Κυρίου ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸν, πῶς εὔχεται ἃ μὴ προσήκει; Ἐνῆν γὰρ καὶ κύνα ἀπαντῆσαι ἐπανιόντι τῷ Ἰεφθάε. Ἆῤ οὖν ἐσφάλη τὸ Πνεῦμα; οὐδαμῶς· ἀλλὰ τὸ μὲν Πνεῦμα βοηθεῖν παραγέγονεν, οὐχ ὑποβάλλειν τὴν ἄτοπον εὐχήν· αὐτὸς δὲ σφάλλεται ἀπερισκέπτως ὑποσχόμενος.
thought_title: The Spirit helped Jephthah but did not prompt his rash vow
orientation: Origen opens his commentary on Judges by asking how the Spirit of the Lord could be upon Jephthah when he made an unfitting vow.
pass_a_gloss: And Jephthah vowed to the Lord. If the Spirit of the Lord was upon him, how does he vow things that are not fitting? For it was possible even for a dog to meet Jephthah as he was returning. Did the Spirit then make a mistake? By no means; but the Spirit came to help, not to suggest the absurd vow; but he himself makes a mistake by promising rashly.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'vow' for εὐχή, not 'oath' or 'prayer'.
The glossary requires this exact rendering for Πνεῦμα Κυρίου.
ἄτοπος means 'out of place' or 'absurd'; 'absurd' captures the sense of an unfitting vow.
The adverb means 'without looking around' or 'without consideration'; 'rashly' fits the context of an unconsidered promise.

pass_b_english: And Jephthah made a vow to the Lord (Judges 11:30). If the Spirit of the Lord was upon him, how could he vow what was not fitting? For a dog could have met Jephthah as he returned. Did the Spirit make a mistake, then? Not at all. The Spirit came to help, not to suggest the absurd vow. Jephthah himself made the mistake by promising rashly.

last_rejected.quote: And Jephthah made a vow to the Lord
last_rejected.why: Greek εῦξατο means “prayed”, not “made a vow”.
last_rejected.fix: And Jephthah prayed to the Lord.
last_rejected.ruling: εὔχομαι includes 'vow' as a standard sense; context of Jephthah's vow (Judg 11:30) confirms it.

last_rejected.quote: how could he vow what was not fitting?
last_rejected.fix: how does he pray for things that are not fitting?
last_rejected.ruling: εὔχομαι can mean 'vow'; context confirms. Translation within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: Did the Spirit make a mistake, then?
last_rejected.why: Greek ἐσφάλη means “was killed/destroyed”, not “made a mistake”.
last_rejected.ruling: σφάλλω commonly means 'make a mistake/err'; 'was killed' is not the standard sense here.

problems.quote: For a dog could have met Jephthah as he returned
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if this is Origen's own illustration or an imagined objector's challenge.
problems.fix: Mark as Origen's hypothetical illustration or an objector's challenge.
